definition: A constitutional principle derived from the First Amendment that prohibits civil courts from deciding disputes that would require them to interpret religious doctrine, resolve questions of church governance, or second-guess the disciplinary decisions of religious organizations. It is rooted in the idea that government—including the judiciary—should stay out of the internal affairs of churches and religious bodies.
examples: In this case, the Missionaries argue that Kentucky courts cannot evaluate whether their reasons for dismissing Frederic were legitimate because doing so would require examining religious doctrine and internal church governance.
